newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened slightly against the basket of foreign currencies and closed almost unchanged against the dollar in mixed trading, dealers said.
"Trading was mixed and quiet with slightly more conversions of shekels into foreign currency. Because of that the basket rose slightly," a dealer said.
"The Bank of Israel was not seen in the market and the representative rate of the basket was set at 6.96 percent below the midpoint of the trading band," he said.

The shekel is allowed to trade in a band of seven percent above or below a sloping midpoint designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.1920 against 3.1910 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5633 shekels against 3.5614 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8690 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8600 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.0861 shekels per mark against 2.0851 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1910 shekels.
